subject: AI & Agents
title: AI-Generated Visual Effects
description: A 60-second lesson on AI-Generated Visual Effects.

hook.text: De-aging Robert De Niro in The Irishman took months. AI can now do it in hours.

buildup.text: AI tools automate rotoscoping, face replacement, background generation, and color grading.

discovery.text: Neural radiance fields (NeRFs) can reconstruct 3D scenes from a handful of photos.

twist.text: VFX artists fear AI will eliminate entry-level positions that train the next generation.

climax.text: Studios see 10x cost savings. Artists see their craft being commoditized.

punchline.text: The magic stays on screen. The magicians worry about their jobs.

quiz.question: How is AI changing visual effects in film?
options: Automating tasks like de-aging, rotoscoping, and scene generation
Replacing all actors with AI characters

details.summary: AI is transforming visual effects by automating rotoscoping, compositing, and scene generation. Tasks that once took teams of artists weeks can now be accomplished in hours with machine learning.
details.whyItMatters: AI VFX tools lower costs and speed up production, making high-quality effects accessible to independent filmmakers. This democratization reshapes the entertainment industry.
takeaways: AI automates labor-intensive VFX tasks like rotoscoping
Production timelines shrink from weeks to hours
Independent filmmakers gain access to blockbuster-level effects

faq.question: Which visual effects tasks has AI automated?
faq.answer: AI now handles rotoscoping, background replacement, de-aging, motion capture cleanup, and scene extension. These were traditionally the most time-consuming parts of post-production.

faq.question: Will AI replace VFX artists entirely?
faq.answer: Unlikely in the near term. AI handles repetitive tasks while artists focus on creative direction and complex shots. The role is shifting from manual execution to creative supervision.
